I am a Principal Machine Learning Engineer with more than a decade of experience
designing, building and operating production-grade ML systems across
manufacturing, industrial, energy and semiconductor domains. My work spans the
full arc of a machine learning project: framing the problem, building the model,
engineering the pipeline and keeping it honest in production. This book follows
that arc, from Python fundamentals to systems that run.

At [Analog Devices](https://www.analog.com) I design and run machine learning
systems for supply chain planning and intelligent edge products, taking ideas
from early prototypes to reliable production systems. I care about clean
architecture, robust deployment, and monitoring and governance once systems are
live, and I work with business and product leaders to align technology roadmaps
and AI investments with the value they are meant to create.

Alongside my industry role I am active in research on time series analysis and
forecasting, mostly for power systems, from non-intrusive load monitoring to
probabilistic net-load forecasting for low-voltage networks, with 10+
peer-reviewed papers in IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid, IEEE Transactions on
Power Systems and IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics. I collaborate
with [Lucas Pereira](https://www.alspereira.info/) at ITI, LARSyS, Técnico
Lisboa.

My open-source work includes [Twiga](https://github.com/sambaiga/twiga) for
point and probabilistic forecasting, Milia for load profiles, Popo for network
simulation, [MLPForecast](https://github.com/sambaiga/mlpforecast) for
uncertainty-aware net-load forecasting and
[Deep-NILMtk](https://github.com/BHafsa/Deep-NILMtk), a community deep learning
toolkit for non-intrusive load monitoring.
